Chapter 11: Living with Intention—Aligning Actions with Values.
Have you ever noticed how life can slip into autopilot? You wake up, head to work, eat, sleep—then do it all over again. Day after day, the routine just keeps rolling. But beneath all that, there’s this quiet longing most of us feel—a desire for meaning, for our actions to actually reflect what we care about deep down.
Let me share a story. Imagine someone who’s seen as successful—a mid-career professional with a packed schedule, always on the move. But despite all the accomplishments, they start to feel empty. One evening, they decide to pause and actually write down what matters most to them: family, creativity, kindness, health. Looking at that list, it hits them—most of their time goes to things that don’t really line up with those values.
That’s what living with intention is all about—making choices that actually match what’s important to you. And here’s the thing: you don’t need to turn your life upside down. Usually, it’s those small shifts that make a real difference. Think about a parent who wants more time with their kids. Instead of scrolling through their phone at dinner, they put it away. Suddenly, the conversations get deeper, and the family starts feeling more connected.
Most of us don’t even realize just how much of our lives are shaped by habits we barely think about. But when you pause and ask yourself, “What do I actually value?” or, “What do I want to nurture in my life?”—things start to get clearer. I have a friend who’s really passionate about the environment. They started biking to work and cutting down on waste. The changes weren’t huge, but you could see the satisfaction on their face—they felt genuinely aligned with what matters to them.
Living with intention also means learning to say no to things that don’t serve you. Picture a volunteer, stretched thin by too many commitments. Once they learned to step back from projects that just drained their energy, they suddenly had time for causes that truly inspired them.
Now, let’s be honest—intentional living isn’t about getting it perfect. There’ll be days when old habits sneak back in, or when your values get lost in the rush. But every single time you pause, and make a choice with awareness, that sense of purpose gets a little stronger.
Over time, living with intention turns into something more than just a practice—it becomes a way of being. Life feels less scattered, your heart feels fuller, and what used to be a blur of constant activity starts to feel like a meaningful journey, shaped by what matters most to you.
